title: Chesterfield and the integrated Mildred Bailey Show: going to the union
summary: The agency would not allow the Black musicians on the Chesterfield program; Maxwell goes to union boss Feinberg and the show is integrated, with threats and bribe offers.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: incident, I don't know if you heard about it, when we were doing the Mildred Bailey Show. We had Charlie Shavers, Teddy Wilson, Al Hall, Specs Powell and Trummy Young.

1944. And Chesterfield -- '45. Chesterfield took the program over and they said -- not Chesterfield, Shube or somebody, the band leader or the advertising agency said, well, this is a Southern company, we can't have a mixed band for a Southern tobacco company. And we'll sneak them in later, in the back door.

So one day Teddy said -- Teddy and I used to be very good friends. And he said, "Are you going to do Chesterfield?" I said, "Sure, aren't you?" And he said, "No," and he got a funny look and he told me the story. So I called up the leader and said, "Look, I can't do it if my friends can't do it. I don't want to do it." And then I got thinking, Jesus, that's not really enough.

So I went up to the union, Willy Feinberg, he was a very militant guy, very leftist. Everybody was a little left then. And I told him the whole story and he got Schube down, Hailey, the guy from MCA who was Shriver, whoever was head of MCA. And he chewed them out. He said, "I'll take off every band off of CBS, I'll close every ballroom that uses an MCA band. You guys are out of work unless these guys start the show.
Well, I got threats to kill me, I got -- Martin Block wanted to bribe me $1,000.00. And, you know, even my friends said, 'You know, you're crazy. Your wife is pregnant and you sacrifice your career.'
